name: Indian Museum
summary: Widely regarded as India's oldest and largest museum, with collections across archaeology, art, anthropology, geology and zoology.

name: National Museum
summary: The flagship national museum under the Ministry of Culture, with art and artefacts spanning thousands of years of Indian history.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya (CSMVS)
summary: Formerly the Prince of Wales Museum; a landmark Indo-Saracenic building holding art, archaeology and natural history collections.

name: Salar Jung Museum
summary: One of the world's largest single-person collections of antiquities, assembled by the Salar Jung family and opened to the public in 1951.

name: National Museum of Natural History
summary: National museum of natural history under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, focused on biodiversity and conservation education.

name: Victoria Memorial Hall
summary: A marble monument-museum set in landscaped grounds, with galleries on the history of Kolkata and British India and a rich collection of paintings.

name: Government Museum, Chennai
summary: One of India's oldest museums, famed for its Chola bronze collection, archaeology and natural history galleries in Egmore.

name: Albert Hall Museum
summary: Rajasthan's oldest museum, housed in an Indo-Saracenic building in Ram Niwas Garden with decorative arts, miniatures and textiles.

name: Mehrangarh Museum
summary: A fort museum run by the Mehrangarh Museum Trust, displaying royal palanquins, arms, paintings, textiles and period rooms.

name: Archaeological Museum, Sarnath
summary: An ASI site museum that houses the Lion Capital of Ashoka, India's national emblem, along with Buddhist sculpture from Sarnath.

name: Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Mumbai City Museum
summary: Mumbai's oldest museum, originally the Victoria and Albert Museum, restored and reopened in 2008 with a focus on the city's history and decorative arts.

name: Napier Museum
summary: An art and natural history museum in a distinctive Indo-Saracenic building, known for its bronzes, ivory carvings and temple artefacts.

name: Calico Museum of Textiles
summary: A museum of Indian textiles and craft traditions established by the Sarabhai family, visited by guided tour.

name: National Gandhi Museum
summary: Museum and library near Raj Ghat devoted to the life and ideas of Mahatma Gandhi, with photographs, personal belongings and archives.

name: Nehru Memorial Museum & Library
summary: Housed in Teen Murti House, it combines a museum, a research library and a major archive of private papers on modern Indian history.

name: Assam State Museum
summary: State museum with archaeology, ethnography, manuscripts and art of Assam and the wider North East.

name: Bihar Museum
summary: A modern state museum opened in 2017 with a children's gallery and galleries on Bihar's ancient and modern history.

name: Visvesvaraya Industrial & Technological Museum
summary: A science and technology museum with hands-on galleries on engineering, electronics, and industrial history.

name: National Handicrafts and Handloom Museum (Crafts Museum)
summary: Showcases the living craft traditions of India with textiles, folk art, ritual objects and a village complex with craftspeople at work.

name: Partition Museum
summary: A people's museum in the Town Hall building that documents the 1947 Partition through oral histories, objects and documents.

name: DakshinaChitra
summary: A living-history museum of the arts, crafts and architecture of South India, with relocated heritage houses and craft demonstrations.

name: National Rail Museum
summary: Open-air and indoor museum of Indian Railways heritage, with historic locomotives, coaches and models in Chanakyapuri.

name: Raja Dinkar Kelkar Museum
summary: A museum built around the personal collection of Dinkar Kelkar, presenting everyday objects, musical instruments, textiles and decorative arts of India.

name: National Museum of Indian Cinema
summary: Run by the Films Division, it traces the history of Indian cinema through galleries, equipment, posters and interactive displays.

name: Museum of Art & Photography (MAP)
summary: A private non-profit museum in Bengaluru bringing together historical and contemporary art, photography, textiles and design with a strong digital programme.

name: Government Museum, Mathura
summary: Home to major collections of Mathura-school sculpture, including Kushan and Gupta period works.

name: National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi
summary: India's premier national gallery of modern and contemporary art, in the former Jaipur House near India Gate.

name: National Gallery of Modern Art, Mumbai
summary: The Mumbai branch of NGMA, housed in the former Sir Cowasji Jehangir Public Hall, hosting modern and contemporary exhibitions.

name: National Gallery of Modern Art, Bengaluru
summary: The Bengaluru branch of NGMA, set in the historic Manikyavelu Mansion, presenting modern and contemporary Indian art.

name: Lalit Kala Akademi
summary: India's national academy of fine arts, organising exhibitions, awards and the Rabindra Bhavan galleries.

name: Kiran Nadar Museum of Art
summary: A private art museum with a collection of modern and contemporary South Asian art and a regular exhibition programme.

name: Jehangir Art Gallery
summary: A long-running Kala Ghoda gallery that has hosted generations of Indian artists since the early 1950s.

name: Academy of Fine Arts, Kolkata
summary: A Kolkata art institution with galleries, a permanent collection and regular exhibitions of Bengal artists.

name: Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath
summary: An art school and gallery complex with the Venkatappa Art Gallery and collections of folk and contemporary art.

name: Gallery Chemould Prescott Road
summary: One of India's oldest contemporary art galleries, showing modern and contemporary artists.

name: Dhoomimal Gallery
summary: A Connaught Place gallery in operation since 1936 and a long-standing part of Delhi's art scene.

name: Nature Morte
summary: A contemporary art gallery founded in 1982 that has shown Indian and international artists.

name: Jawahar Kala Kendra
summary: A multi-arts centre in Jaipur designed by Charles Correa, with galleries, performance spaces and a library.

name: Kochi Biennale Foundation
summary: The organisation behind the Kochi-Muziris Biennale, India's largest contemporary art exhibition, based in Fort Kochi.

name: National Library of India
summary: India's largest library by volume and the library of legal deposit, tracing its roots to the Imperial Library of 1836.

name: Delhi Public Library
summary: A major public library system for Delhi, started as a UNESCO pilot project in public library development.

name: Raja Rammohun Roy Library Foundation
summary: The national agency for public library promotion and support under the Ministry of Culture.

name: The Asiatic Society, Kolkata
summary: Founded by William Jones, it holds rare manuscripts, books, coins and paintings, and is an Institution of National Importance.

name: Connemara Public Library
summary: One of India's four National Depository Libraries, housed in a historic building in Egmore.

name: Thanjavur Maharaja Serfoji's Sarasvati Mahal Library
summary: A historic library of palm-leaf and paper manuscripts from the Nayak and Maratha periods, open as a public library since 1918.

name: Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library
summary: An Institution of National Importance known for its Arabic, Persian and Urdu manuscripts and rare Islamic art.

name: Rampur Raza Library
summary: A national institution housing rare manuscripts, miniature paintings and calligraphy, founded by the Nawabs of Rampur.

name: Library of Tibetan Works and Archives
summary: Founded to preserve Tibetan manuscripts, texts and culture, it houses a library, a museum and an archive.

name: Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute
summary: A research institute with a renowned manuscript library; it produced the critical edition of the Mahabharata.

name: Anna Centenary Library
summary: A large modern public library in Kotturpuram with extensive lending, reference and children's sections.

name: State Central Library, Thiruvananthapuram
summary: One of India's oldest public libraries, tracing its origin to the Trivandrum Public Library of 1829.

name: David Sassoon Library & Reading Room
summary: A Victorian Gothic subscription library in Kala Ghoda, a heritage building with a garden reading room.

name: Goa State Central Library
summary: The state's central library in the capital, with a long history that goes back to the early 19th century.

name: Roja Muthiah Research Library
summary: A research library focused on Tamil studies, with books, periodicals and ephemera preserved and digitised.

name: Asiatic Society of Mumbai
summary: A learned society based in the Town Hall, with a library of rare books and manuscripts including an early Dante edition.

name: National Archives of India
summary: The custodian of the non-current records of the Government of India, with a public search portal and a large research room.

name: Maharashtra State Archives
summary: One of India's oldest record offices, with Bombay Presidency records and Maratha-era documents.

name: Tamil Nadu Archives
summary: Records of the Madras Presidency and Tamil Nadu government, going back to the early 19th century.

name: Telangana State Archives and Research Institute
summary: Holds records of the Nizam's government, Persian-language farmans and Deccan-era documents.

name: Rajasthan State Archives, Bikaner
summary: Preserves the records of former princely states of Rajasthan, including Bikaner's court documents.

name: Historical Archives of Goa
summary: The archives of the Estado da India under Portuguese rule, with centuries of administrative records.

name: National Film Archive of India
summary: Collects and preserves Indian film and film-related material, and runs screenings and film appreciation programmes.

name: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
summary: A national arts centre with major archives, a library, a gallery and a research programme on the arts and culture of India.

name: Sangeet Natak Akademi Archives
summary: The national academy for music, dance and drama, holding a major audio-visual archive of performing arts.

name: Indian Culture Portal
summary: A Ministry of Culture platform that brings together digitised collections from libraries, archives and museums across India.

name: Tata Central Archives
summary: The corporate archive of the Tata group, holding historical papers, photographs and artefacts of Indian industrial history.
